<description>
**Problem:** Processes connected to `bitcoin-node` over IPC (with `-ipcbind`) can use the `Mining` interface, but they can't currently use the `Chain` interface read chain data or follow chain events. Chain data could be useful to third-party clients and Bitcoin Core's own wallet could use this as well to run in a separate process (#10102). But exposing all of `interfaces::Chain` to external clients would make its methods hard to change, since the wallet uses them as internal API (#34981).

**Solution:** Add capnp wrappers for `interfaces::Chain`, split into two interfaces backed by the same C++ class:

- `Chain`, returned by `Init.makeChain`, is stable. It follows Cap'n Proto schema evolution rules, so existing clients keep working as methods are added. It starts with the five block lookup methods: `findBlock`, `findFirstBlockWithTimeAndHeight`, `findAncestorByHeight`, `findAncestorByHash` and `findCommonAncestor`.
- `UnstableChain`, returned by `Init.makeUnstableChain`, extends `Chain` with every other method, for Bitcoin Core's own clients. It can change in any way between releases. Incompatible changes renumber `makeUnstableChain`, so old clients get an error instead of calling the wrong methods.

Methods can move from `UnstableChain` to `Chain` once we're willing to support them for external use. `test/functional/interface_ipc.py` shows a Python client calling both interfaces. Like the existing IPC interfaces, these are only available to processes that can connect to the IPC socket, which already grants full node access through `Init.makeRpc`.

**Merge order:** This depends on bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#377 and bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#379 and a subtree update that includes them (this PR currently carries that bump, plus a `-Wc++23-lambda-attributes` build fix that goes with it), and on #36520, which fixes node crashes IPC clients could trigger with invalid `Chain` arguments.

---

This PR is part of the [process separation project](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/28722).

ef56e411dd build: suppress -Wc++23-lambda-attributes in warn_interface

Lambda [[noreturn]] attributes before the parameter list are a C++23
extension intentionally used in C++20 builds (needed for compatibility
with -Wmissing-noreturn). Suppress the extension warning rather than
removing the attributes or working around them.

Uses the existing IF_CHECK_PASSED idiom so GCC, which silently ignores
unknown -Wno-* flags, is unaffected.

This change was written with Claude Sonnet 4.6.

cd39ed2a6b ipc: Add capnp serialization code for bitcoin types

Add helper functions and type conversions needed by the Chain capnp
interface:

- Add ToBlob, ToArray, Serialize, and Unserialize helper functions
- Add util::Result and util::Expected serialization, using new common.capnp
  Result, ResultVoid, and Expected structs
- Add UniValue::type_error exception serialization
- Add common.capnp BilingualStr and Pair structs

2628ad9d17 ipc: Add capnp wrapper for Handler interface

def23a5e2c interfaces, refactor: Change Chain method signatures for IPC wrappers

Drop const from Chain::getFeeRateEstimate() and
Chain::maximumFeeEstimationTargetBlocks(), and pass the
Chain::updateRwSetting() update function by value, so libmultiprocess can
generate an IPC client class implementing them. Generated client methods are
never const, so they can't override const virtual methods, and the generated
server code can only pass a callback argument to the implementation by value.

abb3f5e86f ipc: Add capnp wrappers for stable Chain and UnstableChain interfaces

Add a stable Chain capnp interface for external clients, and an UnstableChain
interface extending it for Bitcoin Core's own clients, both backed by the C++
interfaces::Chain class. Stable Chain methods follow Cap'n Proto schema
evolution rules so existing clients keep working as methods are added.
UnstableChain methods can change in any way between releases, as discussed in
bitcoin/bitcoin#34981.

The stable interface starts out with only the block lookup methods that use
FoundBlockParam/FoundBlockResult (findBlock, findFirstBlockWithTimeAndHeight,
findAncestorByHeight, findAncestorByHash, findCommonAncestor). Other methods
can be moved to it from UnstableChain when they are ready for external use.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context).

0928430e16 ipc: Expose Chain interface

Add Init.makeChain and Init.makeUnstableChain methods returning the stable
Chain and UnstableChain interfaces to external processes spawning or
connecting to bitcoin-node, and test them in interface_ipc.py.

This change was written with Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context).

The `ProxyServer` objects are just used internally by the `mp::ServeStream(loop, socket, wrapped_object)` and `mp::ListenConnections(loop, socket, wrapped_object[, max_connections])` functions, and aren't exposed externally. The `ProxyClient` classes are exposed, and returned from the `mp::ConnectStream(loop, socket)` function and meant to be used directly. The classes implement methods described in `.capnp` definitions, and whenever any method is called, a request with the method arguments is sent over the associated IPC connection, and the corresponding `wrapped_object` method on the other end of the connection is called, with the `ProxyClient` method blocking until it returns and forwarding back any return value to the `ProxyClient` method caller.
 
+## Event loop
+
+Making connections and IPC calls requires an `mp::EventLoop` instance running in its own dedicated thread. The event loop is reference-counted, and `EventLoop::loop()` returns when the last `mp::EventLoopRef` is released. Therefore, any code that needs to use the loop across multiple calls should maintain its own `EventLoopRef`. Connection objects and proxy objects automatically hold a reference for as long as they exist.
